text:
Ravi S: quick postmortem-style bring-up note for kalypso12 (12B) comparing a dynamic mixed-fleet: baseline all-int8 vs strategy: int6 default + latency-aware bump-to-int8 for long requests. 8k webchat sample. TL;DR: ~25% spend reduction, small QA hit concentrated on high-ambiguity summaries, latency SLO preserved with bump policy.

Camille: paste top-line metrics please.

eval-bot: summary: n=8000, cost_delta=-25% (dynamic vs all-int8), QA_acc_delta=-1.3pp, halluc_delta=+1.4pp, p95_latency_delta=+3ms, bump_rate=18%

Ravi S: compact table:
```
variant                 cost_per_1k  QA_acc  halluc_rate  p95_latency
kalypso12-int8-baseline $0.86        83.9%   2.5%         210ms
kalypso12-dynamic       $0.64        82.6%   3.9%         213ms
```

Derek: where are failures concentrated? any particular slice?

Ravi S: mostly abstractive long summaries and multi-turn clarification flows. short Q&A, code tasks, and template replies are within ~0.3pp. Bump-to-int8 triggers on tokens>1400 OR estimated decode_time>180ms.

Marta: product/GTN ask: what's recommended rollout and unit econ? Also how risky is customer-facing longform?

Ravi S: proposed rollout: conservative hybrid. Default int6 for short endpoints, bump-to-int8 on long/slow requests. Start 2% canary -> 15% over 10 days. Gates: hallucination_rate absolute >4% OR QA_slice_delta >2pp on priority slices OR bump_rate deviates >5pp from sim. Fallback: revert to all-int8 routing if gate trips.

Ravi S: unit-econ quick calc (assume avg tokens/req=1.45k):
- baseline all-int8: cost_per_1k=$0.86 -> cost_req~$1.25 -> per_1M_req~$1,250
- dynamic (18% bump): effective cost_per_1k~$0.64 -> cost_req~$0.93 -> per_1M_req~$930
- savings ~= $320 per 1M reqs (~25.6%)

Camille: callouts: numbers assume same prompt distribution; if product increases context or priming tokens, bump_rate will rise and savings shrink. Also increased observability needed to track bump_rate, per-slice hallucination and per-variant billing.

Derek: mitigations tested: 1) stricter bump threshold (reduce bump_rate to 10%) -> saves less (~18%) but halves halluc delta; 2) selective rerank on bumped outputs -> reduces halluc by ~1.2pp at +4% cost; 3) apply additional grounding prompts for long summaries -> recovers ~0.5pp.

Marta: can you provide a one-paragraph exec blurb for GTN? they want customer-safe wording + unit econ.

Ravi S: draft blurb: "Recommend piloting a conservative dynamic-fleet: int6 by default with an automatic bump to int8 for long or slow requests. In simulation this strategy reduced model spend by ~25% while preserving latency SLOs and keeping longform quality near acceptable thresholds; we observed small hallucination upticks concentrated on abstractive long summaries. Start with a 2% canary and expand to 15% with tight gates (hallucination, QA-slice regressions, bump rate). Revert to all-int8 if guardrails are violated."

Derek: ops owners: add billing tag `variant=kalypso12-dynamic`, emit metrics bump_rate, per-variant p95, and per-slice hallucination. Add alert: hallucination>4% sustained 5m or bump_rate > 25% sustained 10m.

Marta: product will review wording and confirm canary % (likely 2->15). Also request including top-50 failure examples for GTN.

Ravi S: uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-eval/kalypso12/4012345678/ (per-slice CSV, sim config, top-50 failures). Will paste doc link when live.

Camille: +1. I'll help wire the canary smoke harness for bump_rate and halluc metrics.

Derek: noted. If canary trips we roll back and run a short blameless triage.

Ravi S: thanks team, will follow up with per-slice tables and the sim script used.
